title: The Number Vault
description: A vault full of number riddles: disguised amounts, reversed digits, patient snails and a final wall of toggling locks.

questions.prompt: Three little chests held four coins each. A magpie carried off two coins in total. How many coins are still in the chests?
questions.hint: Find the combined starting amount before accounting for what left.
questions.explanation: The chests held 3 × 4 = 12 coins. Removing two leaves 10.

questions.explanation: After seven nights it is 7 metres up. Its climb on day 8 takes it straight to the top.

questions.prompt: I am a two-digit number. My digits add to 9. Reverse them and the number decreases by 27. What am I?
questions.hint: Reversing two digits changes the value by nine times their difference.
questions.explanation: The digits sum to 9 and differ by 3, so they are 6 and 3. Since reversal makes the number smaller, the original is 63.

questions.prompt: A pouch holds 12 tokens, each gold or silver. Gold tokens are worth 3 points and silver tokens 1 point. The pouch is worth 32 points. How many gold tokens are there?
questions.hint: Start by imagining that every token has the lower value.
questions.explanation: Twelve silver tokens would be worth 12 points. Each replacement by gold adds 2 points, so the extra 20 points require ten gold tokens.

questions.hint: Look for the first time that is a whole multiple of all three intervals.
questions.explanation: The least common multiple of 4, 6 and 9 is 36. At 18 the four-minute bell does not ring; at 24 the nine-minute bell does not ring.

questions.prompt: A basket holds more than 10 counters. Grouping them in twos leaves 1 over, in threes leaves 2 over, and in fives leaves 4 over. What is the smallest possible number of counters?
questions.hint: Add one counter mentally and see what happens to every remainder.
questions.explanation: One extra counter would make the total divisible by 2, 3 and 5. Their least common multiple is 30, so the smallest original total is 29.

questions.explanation: Before each payment the traveller held twice the amount left plus two. Working backwards from 1 gives 4, then 10, then 22 coins.

questions.prompt: One of three chests hides a jewel, equally likely in each. You choose one. A keeper who knows its location ALWAYS opens a different, empty chest and offers a switch to the other unopened chest. What is the chance of winning if you always switch?
questions.hint: The keeper's action is guaranteed, not a lucky discovery of an empty chest.
questions.explanation: Switching wins exactly when the original choice was wrong. That happens in two of the three equally likely jewel locations.

questions.prompt: There are 100 closed locks numbered 1 to 100. On pass 1 you toggle every lock, on pass 2 every multiple of 2, and so on through pass 100. Toggling changes open to closed or closed to open. How many locks finish open?
questions.hint: Pair each divisor of a lock's number with the divisor it multiplies by.
questions.explanation: A lock stays open only if toggled an odd number of times. Divisors pair up except at perfect squares, and there are ten squares from 1 through 100.
